:::{#def-linear-code}
#### Linear code

Let the alphabet be a finite field $\ffield{q}$,
such as $\ffield{2} = \set{0, 1}$ with addition and multiplication modulo 2.
A **linear code** is a [block code](#def-block-code)
whose [set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set) of codewords $C$ is a $k$-dimensional [subspace](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-subspaces.html#def-subspace) of $\ffield{q}^n$.
One way to describe it is by a **parity-check matrix**:
an $(n - k) \times n$ [matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) $H$ with
[rank](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-subspaces.html#def-rank) $n - k$ and
$C = \set{y \in \ffield{q}^n : H y = 0}$,
where $y$ is treated as a [column vector](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-column-vector).
A linear code with [block length](#def-block-code) $n$, [dimension](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-subspaces.html#def-dimension) $k$
and [minimum distance](#def-hamming-distance) $d$
is called an $\codeparams{n}{k}{d}{q}$ code.

:::
